title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is not original Grothendieck mathematics. It is a typescript copy of what is almost certainly a pre-publication version of Deligne's 'Courbes elliptiques: formulaire (d'après J. Tate)', published in Modular Functions of One Variable IV, LNM 476 (1975). The section numbering, Tate's change-of-variables formula (1.2), the normal forms (6.1), (6.3), (6.7), (6.8) and the invariants c4, c6 all match that text. The copy carries Grothendieck's annotations. Those visible nearby are the marginal remark on (I) on the previous page and the '?' against (V); the next page adds a fragmentary 'Cor: pour S plat sur Z, ... [ou seulement 2 et 3 non diviseurs de 0]'.

The page proves Prop. 6.9, which describes the automorphism group scheme of an elliptic curve E/S (curve of genus one without additive fibres).

(I) Suppose c4 and c6 are invertible, so j is not 0 or 1728 fibrewise. Then the normal form (6.3) leaves no automorphisms except ±1.

(II)/(III) Suppose 6 is invertible and use the Weierstrass form (2.1) with invariant differential π. By (2.5) an automorphism is determined by the scalar λ by which it acts on π. A given λ in G_m occurs if and only if c4 = λ^4 c4 and c6 = λ^6 c6. Hence Aut(E) → G_m is a closed immersion. If c4 = 0 the image is μ6; if c6 = 0 it is μ4.

(IV) Take p = 3 and j = 0. Write the curve as y^2 = x^3 + a4 x + a6 with a4 a unit, and apply x = u^2 x' + r, y = u^3 y'. Expanding in characteristic 3 gives u^6 a4' = u^2 a4, hence u^4 = 1. It also gives r^3 + a4 r + a6(1 - u^2) = 0, using u^6 = u^2. The group law is (u', r')(u, r) = (uu', u'^2 r + r'). For y^2 = x^3 - x these conditions become u ∈ μ4 and r ∈ F3. The group is therefore Z/3 ⋊ Z/4, non-abelian of order 12, and the image in G_m is μ4.

(V) Take p = 2 and j = 0, with y^2 + a3 y = x^3 + a4 x + a6 and Tate's substitution with r = s^2. The conditions are u^3 = 1, s^4 + a3 s + a4(1 - u) = 0 and t^2 + a3 t + s^6 + s^2 a4 = 0. Counting solutions gives 3 × 4 × 2 = 24 automorphisms; this group is SL2(F3).

Purpose: to complete the table of normal forms and automorphism groups needed for the moduli of elliptic curves at the primes 2 and 3.
errors: (I) holds only fibrewise, or over a connected base: over a disconnected S one can choose ±1 independently on each component. Grothendieck's marginal note on the previous page, 'vrai seulement en [?] connexe', correctly flags this.
Typos: 'défini' should be 'définit'; 'parleur' should be 'par leur'.
The proof of (I) ('D'après (6.3)') is very terse but correct.
(V) is correct (order 24, the group SL2(F3), image μ3), despite the '?' annotation on the statement. The proof on this page breaks off before the solutions are counted.

ideas.what: Automorphism group scheme of an elliptic curve embeds in G_m via its action on the invariant differential when 6 is invertible; the image is μ2, μ4 or μ6 according to c4, c6.
ideas.modern_name: Aut of elliptic curves / j = 0, 1728 extra automorphisms
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical; scheme-theoretic form in Deligne's Formulaire (after Tate), 1975
ideas.where_published: Deligne, LNM 476 (1975); Silverman, AEC, Ch. III and App. A

ideas.what: Automorphisms of the j = 0 curve in characteristic 3: equations u^4 = 1, r^3 + a4 r + a6(1 - u^2) = 0, giving Z/3 ⋊ Z/4.
ideas.modern_name: Aut(E) for supersingular j = 0 in char 3
ideas.where_published: Deligne LNM 476; Silverman AEC Appendix A

ideas.what: Automorphisms in characteristic 2 at j = 0: u^3 = 1, s^4 + a3 s + a4(1 - u) = 0, t^2 + a3 t + s^6 + s^2 a4 = 0, a group of order 24.
ideas.where_published: Deligne LNM 476; Silverman AEC Prop. A.1.2

deep.surprise_reason: This is a copy of Deligne's Tate formulaire, published in 1975, with standard and correct computations. Grothendieck's only contributions are small marginal remarks: (I) needs a connected base, a '?' on (V), and a flatness corollary on the next page. None of these is new mathematics.
transcription_corrections: '(6.6.)' on the previous page refers to the map Aut(E) → G_m; the stray period is a typo.
Previous-page annotation: '[vrai seulement en fai[?] connexe[?] !]' probably reads 'vrai seulement si S connexe !' or similar.
'défini' should be 'définit', and 'parleur' should be 'par leur' (typos in the original typescript).
